thread:
oliver: Quick sync — I opened a PR that updates the Dedicated provisioning docs with the new autoscale cooldown defaults, isolation label examples, and an SDK snippet for creating scale policies. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4123
raya: Thanks — I'll take a first pass. Can you list the specific things you want covered so I can check off in the PR description? :memo:
oliver: Sure — main items: 1) clarify cooldown and burst behavior in autoscale section, 2) add a short tenant isolation example showing labels and eviction behavior, 3) replace the old JS SDK sample with the new unified SDK pattern, 4) fix two dead links in the handbook that the doc lint flagged.
sasha: FYI one of the dead links is the runbook anchor (handbook -> reserved-pools#eviction). I had to re-anchor it last month; I'll paste the correct link in a sec.
mike: Also flag for legal: the SLA wording changed slightly — we need to avoid implying 100% latency guarantees. Can the PR include the exact SLA phrasing we agreed on in the product doc? I'll paste it if not present.
docs-bot: Link check results: 2 broken links found in docs/dedicated/provisioning.md: line 172 -> /handbook/reserved-pools#eviction (404), line 234 -> /sdk/js#deprecatedCreateScalePolicy (404). Automated suggestions attached.
raya: OK, I'll update the PR checklist with the items and mark the doc-bot suggestions as TODOs. Oliver, can you drop the new SDK example here so I can copy it into the PR? Keep it short.
oliver: Pasting minimal unified SDK pattern we want to use:

```js
// create autoscale policy
const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY});
await client.dedicated.createScalePolicy({
  tenantId: 'tenant-123',
  policy: {
    minGPUs: 1,
    maxGPUs: 8,
    cooldownSeconds: 300,
    burstWindowSeconds: 60,
  }
});
```

raya: Nice, I'll include and tweak variable names. For the isolation example, suggest we show label + eviction-preference comment. e.g.:

```yaml
# tenant manifest snippet
tenant_id: tenant-123
labels:
  isolation: dedicated
  env: prod
# eviction_preference: prefer-non-isolated
```
sasha: Here's the fixed runbook anchor: https://handbook.redwood.ai/reserved-pools#eviction-behavior — replace the old path in the PR.
mike: SLA snippet to paste (copy from product doc): "We aim for 99.9% uptime on Dedicated capacity with best-effort latency SLOs per model class. See SLA matrix for committed latency bounds." Please make sure we don't promise hard latency guarantees.
oliver: Good call, mike. I'll add that exact sentence into the SLA section and link to the SLA matrix page.
raya: Quick question — should we mention fallback model behavior in the provisioning doc (what happens if tenant exceeds quota): autopromote to compatible smaller model or queue? I can add a short bullet.
mike: Add both bullet points: 1) automatic fallback to compatible model variant (cost-optimized) if enabled, 2) queued requests with retry header when no compatible variant is available.
oliver: I'll add a short note and a sample curl that shows the retry header. Raya, once you're done, can you assign PR reviewers: @sasha for handbook links, @mike for SLA phrasing, @docs for final copyedit?
raya: Yep. I'll also run the link checker again locally before merging. Plan: update PR with snippet + anchor fixes + SLA sentence by EOD, request reviews.
sasha: Quick nit — in the isolation example, call out that tenant labels are indexed and used by scale policy routing. One-sentence note should suffice.
oliver: Perfect. Thanks everyone — ping if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
